Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 69, verses 19–24:

Explanation of the words:

Haumu (هاؤم): i.e., take.

Inni zanantu (إني ظننت): i.e., I knew.

Radiyah (راضية): i.e., one whose owner is pleased with it.

Qutufuha daniyah (قطوفها دانية): i.e., what is plucked and gathered of the fruits.

Bima aslaftum (بما أسلفتم): i.e., by what you sent forward.

Fi al-ayyam al-khaliyah (في الأيام الخالية): i.e., the past days.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to establish the creed of resurrection and recompense by explaining what takes place on the Day of Resurrection, so He, exalted is He, says: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: "Here, read my record!"﴾. That is, after the coming of the Lord, blessed and exalted, to judge between people, the records are given out: whoever takes his record in his right hand, and whoever takes his record in his left. As for him who is given his record, which contains his good deeds, in his right hand, he will say in great joy: "Haumu" — i.e., take — "read my record, for it is all bright, with no trace of the blackness of evil deeds." He gives the reason for the soundness of his record from evil deeds by saying: "Inni zanantu" — i.e., I knew — "that I would certainly meet my reckoning." Therefore I did not commit evil deeds. And if something befell me and I committed it through ignorance, I immediately repented of it, so its trace was erased from my soul and nothing was written against me. Almighty God, reporting the effects of his success in the soundness of his record from evil deeds, says: "So he will be in a pleasing life" — i.e., one whose owner is pleased with it, because of its pleasantness and abundance of good — "in a lofty Garden, whose fruits are within reach" — i.e., what is plucked and gathered of them is near at hand, so he obtains it with his hand while reclining on his couches. It is said to them: "Eat and drink with ease for what you have sent forward" — i.e., what you did for yourselves — "in the past days" — i.e., the past days of the worldly life, when they were believers, who fasted and stood in prayer, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The establishment of the creed of resurrection and recompense, that is, belief in the Last Day.

2- The effects of belief in resurrection and recompense are evident in the soundness of the believer's record from evil deeds. He gave the reason for this by saying: "Inni zanantu anni mulaqin hisabiyah" — "I knew that I would meet my reckoning," therefore he did not disobey his Lord.

3- Affirmation of a truth expressed in the common saying: "The world is the field of the Hereafter," that is, whoever works in this world reaps the fruits of his deeds in the Hereafter, good or evil.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 69, verses 38–52:

Explanation of the words:

*Bima tubsirun wa ma la tubsirun* (by what you see and what you do not see): that is, by every creature on earth and in the heavens.

*Innahu la-qawlu rasulin karim* (indeed it is the word of a noble messenger): that is, the Qur'an, conveyed by a noble messenger, who is Muhammad (ﷺ).

*Wa ma huwa bi-qawli kahin* (and it is not the word of a soothsayer): that is, the Qur'an is not the word of a soothsayer, for it contains none of the rhymed prose (saj') of soothsayers.

*La-akhadhna minhu bil-yamin* (We would have seized him by the right hand): that is, by force, or: We would have taken hold of his right hand in order to kill him.

*Thumma la-qata'na minhu al-watin* (then We would have severed his aorta): that is, the sinew of the heart, whose severing causes a person to die.

*Hajizin* (preventers): that is, those who prevent. It is the predicate of *ma*, the negation that operates like *laysa*, and it is in the plural because *ahad* (anyone) indicates plurality, as in *la nufarriqu bayna ahadin min rusulih* (We make no distinction between any of His messengers), whereas *bayn* is only used between two or more.

*Wa innahu la-hasratun 'ala al-kafirin* (and it is indeed a cause of regret for the disbelievers): that is, denial of the Qur'an will be a cause of regret on the Day of Resurrection for those who denied it.

*Wa innahu la-haqqu al-yaqin* (and it is indeed the certain truth): that is, the established truth with certainty, or the true certainty.

*Fa-sabbih bismi rabbika al-'azim* (so glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty): that is, declare your Lord, the Mighty, free of all imperfection, before whose greatness everything is small and insignificant; that is, say: "Glory be to my Lord, the Mighty."

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Most High, *Fa-la uqsimu bima tubsirun wa ma la tubsirun* (So I swear by what you see and what you do not see), mean: the matter is not as you see and say, O deniers. I swear by what you see and what you do not see of the creatures on earth and in the heavens. *Innahu* (indeed it) — that is, the Qur'an — *la-qawlu rasulin karim* (is the word of a noble messenger) — that is, from his Lord, the Most High, namely Muhammad (ﷺ); that is, it is his conveyance and his word to you. *Wa ma huwa bi-qawli sha'ir* (and it is not the word of a poet), as you claim falsely. *Qalilan ma tu'minun* (little do you believe): that is, your faith is little and narrow in scope; had it been broad, it would have been wide enough to accept belief that the Qur'an is the speech of God and His revelation, and that it is not of the genre of poetry, because it differs from poetry in both form and meaning. *Wa ma huwa bi-qawli kahin* (and it is not the word of a soothsayer), *qalilan ma tadhakkarun* (little do you reflect): that is, your reflection is very little. Had you reflected much, you would have known that the Qur'an is not the speech of soothsayers, because it is bound to truth, righteousness and guidance, and because its speaker is far from sin and falsehood, unlike the words of soothsayers, whose warp and weft is falsehood and whose speaker is entirely sin. How can the Qur'an be compared with the speech of soothsayers? And how can the Messenger Muhammad be compared with soothsayers, the brothers of the devils? *Innahu tanzilun min Rabbi al-'alamin* (it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds), O deniers, O the astray.

Another matter: if the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) had fabricated some sayings and attributed them to Us, *la-akhadhna minhu bil-yamin* — that is, We would have seized him and taken hold of his right hand — *thumma la-qata'na minhu al-watin* (then We would have severed from him the aorta), and he would have perished, for the watin is the vein of the heart; when it is severed, a person dies. If We did this to him, who among you could prevent Us from him? This is the meaning of His words, the Most High: *Fa-ma minkum min ahadin 'anhu hajizin* (so none of you could prevent Us from him). His words, the Most High, *Wa innahu* (and indeed it) — that is, the Qur'an — *la-tadhkiratun* (is indeed a great reminder) for the righteous who fear God's punishment and dread His vengeance and torment. *Wa inna lana'lamu anna minkum ayyuha al-nas mukadhdhibin* (We know that among you, O people, are deniers); their condition is not hidden from Us, and We will recompense them for their description. *Wa innahu la-hasratun 'ala al-kafirin* — that is, on the Day of Resurrection, when they see the believers in it taken to the right, to the Abode of Peace, and the deniers taken to the left, to the Abode of Ruin.

*Wa innahu la-haqqu al-yaqin* — that is, the true certainty.

After this affirmation of revelation and prophethood, the Most High commanded His Messenger, whose message was denied by the deniers, to seek help in patience through the remembrance of God, saying to him: *Fa-sabbih bismi rabbika al-'azim* — that is, say: "Glory be to my Lord, the Mighty," declaring His name free of distortion and of naming created things by it, glorifying your Lord to the utmost extent, for He is the Most High, the Mighty.

Guidance from the verses:

1. God may swear by whatever He wills of His creatures for lofty wisdoms, but it is not permitted for a servant to swear by other than the Lord, the Most High.

2. Affirmation of revelation and establishment of Muhammadan prophethood.

3. Describing the Messenger as noble, and his honour before his Lord, the Most High.

4. The Messenger (ﷺ) is incapable of lying about God, the Most High, and would have no ability to do so even if he wished; for one who does not lie to people will not lie about God, as Heraclius said when he rebutted Abu Sufyan, who had said to him: "We have never tested him in a lie." (Heraclius said: "He would not abandon lying to people and then lie about God.")

5. The legitimacy of glorifying with the words "Glory be to my Lord, the Mighty," if it is authentically reported that when this was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: "Make it part of your bowing (ruku')." Thus it became a confirmed sunnah to say "Glory be to my Lord, the Mighty" three times or more in bowing.
